review: P4-B1 independent offline sandbox and migration safety review

initial_findings.problem: Initial code checked only project-labeled volumes and only when no containers existed. An exact deterministic Compose volume name with absent/foreign labels could therefore be adopted, including in a partial owned project.
initial_findings.evidence: Two independent mocked-Docker tests failed before fix: new project and partial owned project both reached Compose up instead of rejecting a foreign exact-name pgdata volume.
initial_findings.resolution: Coordinator checks all exact-name volumes independently of container existence and requires both owner and Compose project labels.

initial_findings.problem: Initial Docker subprocesses inherited ambient interpolation variables and Docker contexts despite validating compose.env. Thus validated manifest values did not guarantee the values applied by Compose.
initial_findings.evidence: Independent ambient PROJECT/OWNER/PG_PASSWORD/port test failed before fix because child env was inherited.
initial_findings.resolution: Coordinator supplies a limited child environment for Docker queries and mutations, and fixes Docker host to the local Unix socket.

initial_findings.problem: Initial migration CLI downgraded to base on every requested roundtrip, while the test module requested roundtrip on every rerun. Existing sandbox schema/data could be dropped despite the initial-only help description.
initial_findings.evidence: Source-verified unconditional upgrade/downgrade/upgrade call sequence; no destructive database experiment performed.
initial_findings.resolution: Coordinator added an initial empty-schema precondition and matching successful-roundtrip marker. Unmarked nonempty DB refuses; valid resumed marker upgrades without downgrade; mismatched marker refuses.

initial_findings.problem: Initial ps accepted any one owned container without confirming all direct manifest endpoints. Partial startup plus an unrelated localhost Redis/Qdrant listener could let subsequent unauthenticated backend probes mutate an unowned service.
initial_findings.evidence: Source-verified missing service completeness and actual binding checks; offline counterexamples verify rejection after fix.
initial_findings.resolution: Coordinator verifies unique service roles, owner/project labels, static loopback ports, expected named data volume, and all three running endpoints with matching actual published ports before ps succeeds.

validation.method: Docker subprocesses entirely replaced with offline inspect/list/run doubles. Temporary synthetic manifests only. Migration metadata probes and Alembic upgrade/downgrade calls replaced with recording doubles; no DB opened.
validation.final_command: conda run --no-capture-output -n adaptive-rag python -m pytest tests/unit/test_p4b_sandbox_review.py -q --basetemp .scratch/p4b-sandbox-review-final --junitxml=research/docs/agent_engineering_upgrade/p4_dependency_integration/evidence/b1_independent_review_green.xml
validation.ruff_command: conda run --no-capture-output -n adaptive-rag python -m ruff check tests/unit/test_p4b_sandbox_review.py
coverage: Reject foreign exact-name pgdata volume with no containers and with partial correctly configured owned containers
Exclude conflicting ambient Compose interpolation values from child environment
Reject partial service set before direct endpoint access
Reject wrong static ports, wrong actual ports, stopped services and unexpected volume mounts
Accept complete correctly owned and bound service set with forced local Docker host
Only empty initial DB permits roundtrip; valid resume marker suppresses downgrade; wrong marker and unmarked nonempty DB refuse
Record fresh upgrade/downgrade/upgrade versus resumed upgrade-only migration call sequence

evidence.initial_harness_error: b1_independent_review_red.xml: three fixture errors from absent scratch parent; no product assertions reached
evidence.initial_counterexamples: b1_independent_review_counterexamples_red.xml: three assertion failures before implementation fixes
evidence.safe_red_confirmation: b1_independent_review_safe_red.xml: same three assertion failures with fixture repr suppressed
evidence.first_followup: b1_independent_review_followup.xml: seven tests passed after coordinator fixes

validation.trace_privacy: Three prepared-fixture repr lines in initial_counterexamples XML were replaced with a redaction marker; they contained freshly generated unused scratch configuration. Assertion messages, test counts and results are preserved. Tests now use a private repr to avoid recording scratch credentials.

strengths: Manifest URLs are reconstructed and matched against unique project, loopback addresses, ports, bounded generated credentials and Compose hash.
Live access requires Linux plus explicit P4B_RUN_LIVE and a manifest within the phase private directory; Windows real-service tests skip with BLOCKED reason.
Compose uses project-scoped names, loopback bindings, per-container/per-volume owner labels and no destructive prune/down-v interface.
Migration config explicitly replaces the Alembic DSN and async Alembic engine disposes in finally.
Outage tests attempt service recovery in finally; real dependency assertions do not count in-memory fallbacks as service integration.

considered_and_set_aside.behavior: Actual Docker Compose startup, ownership inspect schema and stop/start behavior
considered_and_set_aside.reason: Windows stage explicitly prohibits services. Offline tests validate guards with synthetic inspect responses; real compatibility requires Ubuntu B2/B3.

considered_and_set_aside.behavior: Real PostgreSQL roundtrip, transaction/idempotency behavior and restart durability
considered_and_set_aside.reason: No real database actions authorized; migration tests verify control-flow guards only.

considered_and_set_aside.behavior: Redis/Qdrant persistence, dimensions, filter, outage and recovery outcomes
considered_and_set_aside.reason: Prepared live tests were source-reviewed only and remain NOT_RUN/BLOCKED for Windows.

considered_and_set_aside.behavior: Live API worker and harness implementation
considered_and_set_aside.reason: Coordinator explicitly excluded concurrently edited files from this review; this verdict covers the listed B1 files only.

considered_and_set_aside.behavior: Large-scale credential management, hostile local administrator or concurrent out-of-band Docker resource replacement
considered_and_set_aside.reason: Small operator-owned isolated acceptance sandbox; no claim of protection against a privileged local adversary or concurrent administrator actions.

assessment: Bounded B1 preparation safety review passes after the coordinator's fixes. All four identified issues are resolved in source and verified by offline counterexamples. This is not real-service acceptance and does not authorize B2/B3 on Windows.
